deities: Jalandhar Nath Ji (revered Nath guru; the temple was built in his honour)
festivals: Maha Shivaratri (grandly celebrated, with Rajasthani dance and music)

history.summary: Built in 1812 by Maharaja Man Singh of Marwar in honour of his revered guru Jalandhar Nath Ji of the Nath sect. The temple is the main seat (peeth) of the Nath Panth in Rajasthan, with Lord Shiva as the principal deity. It is famous for its hall supported by 84 intricately carved pillars, each depicting yogic postures, mythological scenes, and Rajasthani folk motifs, plus frescoes and fine stone carvings. A government school for underprivileged children now operates on part of the premises, and visitor reports note maintenance concerns. Note: some web sources call it the '900 pillars' temple (airial.travel); 84 pillars is the widely cited figure.

name: Maha Mandir
town_description: Jodhpur, the 'Blue City' and 'Sun City' of Rajasthan, is the historic capital of Marwar founded by Rao Jodha in 1459. Dominated by the massive Mehrangarh Fort, it is Rajasthan's second-largest city and a major tourist hub for Rajput heritage, blue-painted old-town houses, textiles, and handicrafts.

travel.railway: Jodhpur Junction, on the route towards Mandore; easy auto/taxi ride
travel.road: Mahamandir area, Jodhpur (PIN 342006), ~4 km from the old bus stand; reachable by bus, taxi, or auto-rickshaw

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri for the full festival experience
